correctness.rationale: The beta integral gives ||z^k||²=k!/(β+1)_k. The normalized double derivative has t^j coefficient (β+1)_{j+m} binom(j+m,m)^2/(j+m)!, giving the stated prefactor and Euler transform. Pfaff gives Q=(1−t)^m P_m^(0,β)((1+t)/(1−t)); the Cayley map takes positive Jacobi roots precisely into the attainable negative scalar interval (−1,0), excluding x=0. Orthogonality of the divided monic polynomials gives the derivative formula with a positive integrand, also valid near β=0; Legendre parity and the large-β collapse toward x=1 prove all crossings and their simplicity. Directly T_2=(β²−β−4)/2 and T_3=β(−β²+3β+16)/6. In the large-order recurrence, uniform convergence of the off-diagonals applies to the actual entries j=1,...,m−1, not to the artificial a_m=0. At the last row the missing link can only improve the Gershgorin lower bound; the last o(m) but divergent block has the limiting constant coefficients, and alternating sine vectors attain the limiting lower edge. This proves h(c) and by monotonicity the strict two-sided threshold statements. Fixed-order hypergeometric coefficients differ from Laguerre by O_m(β^-1); simplicity and the Cayley map give the stated O_m(β^-2) refinement. Independent bounded replay: python /workspace/reproductions/check.py 4 (252 exact kernel coefficients, m=2,3 crossings, high-order and Laguerre spectrum samples). The finite spectra corroborate but do not prove the limits. The frozen CHECK.py was inspected, not executed.
